question: Packages loans and catalog import each other. For planning changes and releases, how many independent modules are there?
options: Two, because each package has its own folder, __init__.py and test suite
One: modules in a cycle must change and release together
Two, as long as each has its own unit tests
None, because cycles make Python imports fail
explanation: A cycle puts both packages in one strongly connected component (T23.2). Python often tolerates such cycles at import time, which is why they survive.

question: A rule says 'only call your own layer or lower layers'. Does it guarantee there are no dependency cycles?
options: No: modules in the same layer may still import each other
Yes: a layered design is acyclic by definition, whatever the layer rule
Yes, provided there are at least three layers
No, but only when a layer has one module
explanation: Only strict layering (always strictly lower) implies acyclicity (T23.1).

question: The mean latency of POST /loans is 148 ms and the SLO is 'p99 ≤ 300 ms'. Is the SLO met?
options: Yes, because the mean is well below the 300 ms target for this endpoint
Yes, if the median is also below 300 ms
No, because the mean is above 100 ms
You cannot tell from the mean; the percentile must be measured
explanation: In lesson 15 a mean of 147.9 ms hid a p99 of 2846.3 ms: one request in five took about 3 s in the incident window.

question: Two replicas of a 99 % service run behind a load balancer. When is the pair 99.99 % available?
options: Always: two replicas square the unavailability, whatever they happen to share
Only if both run the very same software version
Only if their failures are independent, with no shared cause
Never: replicas cannot raise availability
explanation: 1 − 0.01² assumes independence; a shared database, config or bad deploy breaks it (T24.2, P24-5).

question: A consumer may receive the same LoanCreated event twice. What keeps the read model correct?
options: Rely on the broker's exactly-once delivery setting to prevent all duplicates
Add a retry with exponential backoff in the consumer
Make the handler idempotent, e.g. remember processed event ids
Process events in parallel so duplicates race
explanation: At-least-once delivery means duplicates happen; lessons 9 and 12 make handlers idempotent with the eventId.

question: A provider renames the field title to name. All provider unit tests pass. What catches the break before release?
options: More provider unit tests with higher branch coverage of the serialiser code
A consumer-driven contract test verified against the provider
A load test of the provider at peak traffic
Static type checking inside the provider
explanation: Lesson 14's failure lab: provider unit tests cannot know what consumers rely on; the consumer's contract does.

question: Sizing instances on the average request rate at 100 % utilisation leads to what at peak?
options: Queues grow and tail latency explodes
Slightly higher CPU but unchanged latency
Lower cost with the same p99 latency
Requests are spread evenly, so nothing changes
explanation: In lesson 21 the average-sized plan ran at 135 % utilisation at peak with p99 58 s; headroom and N+1 fix it.

question: Where should the rule 'at most 3 active loans per member' be enforced?
options: In the HTTP handler that receives the request
In the user interface, by disabling the button
In a nightly batch job that fixes violations
In the aggregate root, before any state changes
explanation: Only checks inside the aggregate cover every path that changes its state (T25.1); handlers and UIs can be bypassed.

question: In a shared-schema multi-tenant database, where must the tenant filter live?
options: In the UI, which only ever shows the signed-in user's own library
In the login page, which picks the right library
In a weekly report that flags cross-tenant rows
In every data query, enforced and tested in the data layer
explanation: Lesson 18's failure lab leaked 686 of 700 rows from a report without a tenant filter; the guard belongs where data are read.

question: Where should a service's database password come from?
options: A config file committed next to the code so every environment gets it
A constant in the settings module for easy change
An environment variable or secret store, never the repository
The README, so new developers can start fast
explanation: 12-factor configuration keeps config, especially secrets, out of the code base.

question: A subclass overrides a method so that it raises for inputs the base class accepted. Is it substitutable?
options: Yes: the method name, the parameters and the return type are all unchanged
No: it strengthens the precondition and breaks some correct clients
Yes, if it raises a subclass of the original exception
No, but only when it also changes the return type
explanation: Behavioural subtyping is about contracts, not signatures (T25.2).

question: A model checker reports no violation for a model of the borrow workflow. What does that prove?
options: The property holds for the model within its bounds
The production code can never violate the property
The property holds for any number of members
The database constraints are now redundant
explanation: Model checking proves facts about the model; the link to code needs tests (T25.3, P25-7).

question: A study finds classes with high coupling have more faults. Which explanation must you rule out first?
options: Larger classes have both more coupling and more faults
Coupling directly causes faults in every system
The fault data were collected after release
Coupling was measured by a static tool
explanation: El Emam et al. (2001) showed size confounding can create the whole association.

question: An automated accessibility checker reports no errors on the borrow flow. Does the flow conform to WCAG 2.2 AA?
options: Yes: modern checkers test every WCAG 2.2 success criterion automatically now
Yes, if the checker supports WCAG 2.2 rules
No: checkers only test WCAG 2.0
Not necessarily: many criteria need manual and assistive-technology testing
explanation: Automated tools cover part of WCAG; keyboard and screen-reader testing by people is still required.

question: Three AA failures are known two weeks before launch. What is the honest status statement?
options: State 'WCAG 2.2 AA compliant' now and fix the three failures after launch
Say nothing until the fixes are complete
Name the gaps, the accessible alternative, the owner and the fix date
Call it minor technical debt and move on
explanation: ACM Code 1.3 requires disclosure of limitations; a false conformance claim is a misrepresentation.
